problems.description: Session 1 deletes the entire 200-LOC seeded auth API (index.ts) wholesale and starts a greenfield static site generator, discarding the seed's working baseline, tests, and package scaffolding. This removes the measured anchor that test_executed_success, mutation survival, and basin-escape measurement depend on for the story's later sessions.

40 convention violations (measured convention score 0.53): naming rule breaches in DevServerPlugin.ts, MarkdownPlugin.ts, and TemplatePlugin.ts (Classes/Interfaces should be PascalCase, Constants should be UPPER_CASE).

+89 imports and +10 cognitive complexity for a small static site generator suggest plugin/factoring overhead disproportionate to the task, inflating the module surface the story's later sessions must maintain.

package.json declares a new 'ssg' identity and a fresh gray-matter/marked dependency set while abandoning the seed's existing dependencies, silently rewriting the project contract rather than layering onto it.

strengths: Modular multi-file layout (src/cli.ts + generator + plugins) is a reasonable separation of concerns for a CLI tool.
package.json bin/build/test/prepare wiring is complete and idiomatic for a TypeScript project.
CLI option parsing validates flag arity and prints a usage error on malformed input.
commit_reviews.summary: Grounding in the mechanical measurements: this greenfield Session 1 builds a clean but heavier-than-needed SSG with a low 0.53 convention score and 40 naming violations, at the cost of deleting the entire working seed baseline (architectural fit ~0.45).

problems.description: renderTemplatedPage couples template and layout resolution with nested fallback conditionals (if existsSync → if not page.template → return renderPage / else throw), the main driver of the measured +16 cognitive complexity; the two-layer fallback/render flow could be split into small helpers.

Muddled render context contract: renderTemplate injects both 'body' and 'content' into the same context, and the layout render passes 'content: page.html' even though layouts consume '{{body}}'; the Page & {body?, content?} typing makes the template/layout data contract ambiguous.
No tests cover the error paths introduced (explicit frontmatter template/layout that does not exist → throw) or the default-template-absent fallback to renderPage; only the happy paths are tested.

DISCREPANCY: the measured 0.53 convention score / 40 violations are attributed to DevServerPlugin.ts, MarkdownPlugin.ts, TemplatePlugin.ts — files NOT in this diff (different codebase artifacts). The commit's own additions are conventional (camelCase functions, PascalCase interface Page, consistent node:fs/node:path imports), so the low score does not reflect this commit.

All new templating logic (5 functions, ~70 lines) is concentrated in generator.ts, which is growing into a kitchen-sink module; a dedicated template module would be cleaner, though it respects the existing single-file pattern.

strengths: Backward compatible: defaults ('./templates', template: 'default') preserve the existing renderPage behavior, and a missing default template silently falls back while an explicitly requested missing template throws a clear error.
Well tested: covers both the default template + layout + partials path and frontmatter-selected template/layout rendering, mirroring the existing test structure.
Consistent integration: the --templates CLI flag is threaded through cli.ts → BuildOptions → buildSite and the usage string is updated in the same commit.
Global Handlebars.partials state is reset on each build, avoiding stale-partial leakage across repeated builds in one process.
Clear, specific error messages for missing template/layout paths aid debuggability.
commit_reviews.summary: A coherent, backward-compatible Handlebars templating feature (templates/layouts/partials with frontmatter selection) that fits the existing SSG architecture and is well tested, with only minor debt from a complex nested render flow and an ambiguous template context contract — while the measured low convention score is driven by files outside this diff.

problems.description: The entire point of this session — the dev server — is behaviorally untested: serveFile's path-traversal guard, 403/404 responses, MIME/directory-to-index handling, the debounced rebuild, the WebSocket reload broadcast, and close() have no tests; only the pure injectLiveReload function is covered.
tests/server.test.ts asserts the exact full live-reload script string; any change to the injected HTML breaks the assertion (brittle golden-string test).

serveFile + startServer concentrate the measured +29 cognitive complexity; also buildSite() rmSyncs outputDir on every watch-triggered rebuild, which can race in-flight browser requests and cause transient 404s during a rebuild.
Two new runtime deps (chokidar ^4.0.3, ws ^8.18.0) for the dev server; defensible (established libs) but heavier than native fs.watch/http alternatives.

Discrepancy: the measured convention score (0.53) cites violations in DevServerPlugin.ts/MarkdownPlugin.ts/TemplatePlugin.ts, none of which exist in this commit's tree (this cell has only generator.ts/cli.ts/server.ts) — the scan appears to have run against a different/broader tree, so the score under-represents this commit's own conventions.

strengths: Reuses the existing generator API via ServeOptions extends BuildOptions instead of duplicating build logic
Path-traversal protection (resolve + root prefix check) with explicit 403/404 handling in serveFile
injectLiveReload extracted as a pure, exported function and unit-tested; output dir stays clean (injection only at serve time)
CLI stays consistent with the codebase's throw-on-invalid-usage pattern, adds validated --port, and updates the usage message
Debounced rebuild and a graceful close() that tears down the timer, watcher, sockets, and HTTP server
commit_reviews.summary: A well-structured integration session that follows the existing generator/CLI patterns and includes proper security handling, though the mechanical 0.53 convention score is a misattribution (it cites files absent from this diff) and the new server core itself lacks behavioral tests.

problems.description: Module-level mutable `parsedPages` Map in MarkdownPlugin.ts is unbounded global state that persists across builds in the same process; the defensive `tags: [...cached.tags]` clone on both the read and write paths signals the cache must defend against downstream mutation, i.e. shared-mutable-state hazard.

Incremental mode never removes the output directory and skips writing cache-hit pages, so a markdown page deleted from content leaves an orphaned HTML file in outputDir (stale-output correctness gap not covered by the diff).
Cache keys embed the full page source text (`${filePath}\0${source}`) rather than a hash, duplicating content in memory per page; the same source is also independently hashed in generator.ts.

Cache-hit validity checks only sourceHash + templateHash, not plugin or config changes, so cache entries can silently go stale; `parsedPages` re-parses are redundant with the file-based .ssg-cache.json approach.

Build function grew by +26 cognitive complexity and +1 smell as the cache/clean/incremental logic was inlined into build(); `parsedPages` is a lowercase module-level name, matching the pre-existing 'constants should be UPPER_CASE' violation pattern.
No tests added for the new --incremental/--clean cache-hit, template-hash-invalidation, or deleted-page paths; the AST diff shows no new test files.

strengths: Extends the existing BuildPipeline/PluginContext seams (context.file.cacheHit, context.stats) instead of forking a second build path — the caching slots into the plugin architecture cleanly.
Cache-hit pages skip re-render AND re-write, correctly relying on the untouched outputDir state rather than re-emitting files.
Graceful degradation: a missing/corrupt cache or --clean downgrades to a full build, and template hashing over sorted .hbs files is deterministic.
commit_reviews.summary: A reasonable incremental-build feature that rides the existing pipeline/plugin seams, but it ships real technical debt (unbounded module-level parse cache, stale-output risk on deleted pages, +26 cognitive complexity) and its 0.53 convention score is largely inherited from pre-existing violations in untouched files like DevServerPlugin.ts rather than new ones.

compounding_issues: Seed codebase mismatch: Session 1 discarded the entire Express auth-API seed (200 LOC, irrelevant to a static site generator) and rebuilt greenfield, so the baseline was burned rather than built upon

Unverifiable tests throughout: the runtime lacks node/npm/jest/tsc, so every session's `npm test`/`jest`/`tsc` attempts failed and the agent wrote ~11 tests it could never execute (top-level result: test_executed_success=False, test_count=0) — the Session 4 plugin refactor and Session 5 incremental cache were shipped blind
Incremental build never prunes deleted pages: stale .html files linger in outputDir unless --clean is passed, so the cache can serve removed content
Unbounded module-level parsePage memo Map (keyed by path+source) grows forever across rebuilds in a long `serve` session — a memory leak
key_decisions: Discard the irrelevant auth-API seed and build the SSG greenfield in Session 1
Adopt gray-matter + marked for parsing/rendering and a deliberately hand-rolled YAML subset, avoiding a heavyweight YAML dependency
Choose Handlebars for templates with frontmatter-selected template/layout plus partials (Session 2)
Dev-server integration via chokidar file watching + WebSocket live reload with a hand-injected reload script (Session 3)

Restructure everything into a plugin architecture with lifecycle hooks (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) and a ssg.config.ts loaded through a require.extensions TypeScript loader (Session 4) — the most consequential choice, and the heaviest session (42.6k tokens, $0.41)
Add incremental builds keyed by sha256 source+template hashes into .ssg-cache.json with skip/time-saved stats and per-page memoization (Session 5)
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across the five sessions. Sessions 1-2 produced a clean, well-tested core (markdown parsing, templating, CLI); Session 3 added a polished integration layer (watch + live reload); Session 4 was the ambitious, risky pivot — a full plugin-architecture refactor that reshaped every file and slimmed the server from ~94 to ~40 lines while growing the test surface; Session 5 delivered genuine cross-cutting value (incremental caching, build statistics, parse memoization) layered cleanly on the Session 4 pipeline. The test suite grew from 3 to ~11 cases and the architecture matured from a flat script into a lifecycle-driven, configurable pipeline. The persistent weakness is that the environment could never execute TypeScript tooling, so the entire arc — including the two largest changes — was built and committed without a single green test run.
story_review.summary: A textbook greenfield→feature→integration→refactor→cross-cutting arc with strong session-to-session carryover and steadily improving structure, marred only by an environment that made the growing test suite unverifiable and a seed baseline that was wholly discarded.
